$comment: Single source of truth for runtime entitlements. Read by BOTH the daemon
(src/runtime/registry.ts, via a JSON import) and Ansible (include_vars in
the runtime-entitlement role) — same bytes, so the two cannot drift.
A group here means exactly one thing: 'this principal may execute this
runtime series on this host'. Groups are per (runtime, series), not per
runtime: co-installed PHP versions are distinct binaries, so a single
tpphp group would mean granting 8.4 also grants 8.3 with whatever CVEs
another tenant's app is pinned to.
gids are hand-assigned, never computed from the version string — that
breaks the day 8.10 exists. Band 9900-9979 is reserved for entitlement
groups; 9980-9999 is the service-identity band (web-service-user, tp,
tpnodeapp, tpcaddysite). src/orchestration/service-accounts.test.ts
enforces global uniqueness across both.
$accessGroupsComment: SSH access groups. Not entitlement groups, and deliberately not in the
9900-9979 band: an entitlement group protects a binary's mode bits, while
these only select an `sshd` Match block. They live here anyway because
revocation needs ONE containment set — ensurePrincipalManagedGroups removes
stale membership only for names this file defines, so the user's own group, tp, and
anything an operator added by hand are never touched. Two files would mean
two containment sets and a downgrade that leaves a group behind.
One group per access level rather than one 'tpssh' group plus a shell
check: sshd matches on groups, not on shells, so ForceCommand
internal-sftp has to hang off a group of its own. 'password' is not a
level — it is an additive credential group whose Match block turns
PasswordAuthentication on for members; it rides alongside tpsftp/tpshell.
'principal' is not a level either: EVERY principal holds it, whatever its
level, so sshd has one Match block that covers a tenant account with no
SSH access at all. Without it such an account falls through to the host's
global defaults: its own ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and TCP forwarding.

$comment: One group spans both PHP flavors: tpphp84 owns /usr/sbin/php-fpm8.4,
/usr/bin/php8.4, AND vendor/lsphp/8.4/current/bin/lsphp. Semantically
'may execute PHP 8.4 here', whichever engine serves the site.
gids 9906 (8.0) and 9907 (7.4) are held back for the older series the
Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 suites would add (see suiteSeries).
$suiteSeriesComment: PHP series offered per Debian/Ubuntu suite (VERSION_CODENAME), and the
same list for every engine: lsphp (OpenLiteSpeed) and php-fpm (nginx,
Apache). Owner decision 2026-10-07: mirror what the LiteSpeed repository
suite, so web hosting is at parity across engines and server versions.
Debian 13 (trixie) is the only supported OS today, so it is the only
suite listed. Checked 2026-10-07: LiteSpeed also publishes 7.4 and 8.0
for bullseye, bookworm and jammy, 8.1-8.5 for noble, 8.2-8.5 for
resolute; ondrej/sury publishes every one of those series for Debian
(trixie, bookworm, bullseye). A suite is added here only together with
its pinned lsphp digests and the 7.4/8.0 registry series; a test fails
a suite that lists a series the lsphp role cannot install.
Nothing is installed up front: a series lands on the first deploy that
names it and goes when no site uses it any more (series prune).
$builtinExtensionsComment: Extensions compiled into the interpreter for a series: there is no
php<series>-<name> / lsphp<NN>-<name> package to install (PHP 8.5 builds
opcache in), and loading opcache.so from php.ini would fail.
$extensionsComment: Extensions are host-global per series: sury registers them in
there is no per-pool loading. Requests therefore resolve by UNION across
every site on a series — site A gets `intl` because site B asked for it.
That is the honest constraint, and it is exactly why the list is closed.
Excluded on purpose: xdebug (source disclosure + severe perf cost), ffi,
pcntl. Add only with a reason written down.

$comment: Deno publishes one major (2) and ships minors often, so a series is the
major: the vendoring role installs the newest 2.x release and moves
`current` at it. Add a series only when Deno ships a new major.
